key_insight: This MRI study—not cancer drug discovery—uses physics-guided AI to estimate myelin-sensitive macromolecular pool fraction (MPF) from conventional brain scans without paired quantitative reference scans.
clinical_relevance: The approach could enable research into demyelinating pathology using existing MRI archives without dedicated quantitative magnetization transfer acquisitions.
method: Self-supervised learning from conventional T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and FLAIR MRI.
An embedded two-pool magnetization transfer signal model guides MPF estimation.
Acquisition-parameter conditioning accommodates heterogeneous clinical protocols.
evidence_signal: Using 7,705 multisite 3 T MRI sessions, evaluation included 1,237 test sessions; lesions in 70 demyelinating-disease sessions had 35.6% lower MPF than normal-appearing white matter.
watch_item: The abstract does not report validation against quantitative MPF reference scans, and cross-protocol repeatability was assessed in only one healthy volunteer.
paper_title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework
